newsitem.title: GERMANY: German labour chief calls for flexible work hours.
newsitem.headline: German labour chief calls for flexible work hours.

text.p: Germany must adopt more flexible labour laws in order to bring down unemployment from record levels without dismantling its generous social security system, Bernhard Jagoda, president of the Federal Labour Office said on Monday.
More flexible work and production hours would open up new opportunities for employment and lower labour costs, Jagoda said at a conference of the German Civil Servant Association (DBB).
This year "must become the year of mobile work hours," he said, warning that Germany's image as a corporate "purgatory" is pushing investment capital to other countries.
So-called 610-mark jobs, which pay less than the minimum taxable wage, are also no solution. "The social state must be defended," Jagoda said.
